meta.description: Approved plain-language definitions. General explanations only, not personalized advice. The agent selects and offers these; it does not write its own tax or legal rules and does not recommend actions. also_heard_as lists casual phrasings, acronyms, and phonetic/spelled-out variants the agent may map to this term (and must then confirm with the client). source_id and also_heard_as are optional additions.

glossary.plain: A retirement account that holds money moved from an earlier workplace retirement plan.
also_heard_as: retirement money from my old job
the account from my last employer

glossary.plain: A type of retirement account generally funded with money that has already been taxed. Withdrawal rules vary.
Money taken out of a retirement account. Taxes and other rules may apply.
also_heard_as: taking money out of my retirement

glossary.plain: Taking money out of an account. For retirement accounts this is often called a distribution.
An account that holds investments such as stocks, bonds, and funds, without the special rules of a retirement account.
The person or organization you name to receive an account if you pass away.
Moving money or investments from one account to another, at the same firm or a different one.
An amount that the rules say must be taken out of certain retirement accounts each year after a set age. An advisor can explain whether it applies to you.
also_heard_as: the amount I have to take out

glossary.plain: A professional who helps you plan and make decisions about your money and investments.
Someone you name whom the firm may reach out to if it cannot reach you or is concerned about your account. They cannot make changes or trades for you.
also_heard_as: someone you can call about me

glossary.plain: A general measure of how much an investment has gained or lost relative to its cost. This is an explanation of the term, not a statement about your accounts.
A retirement account often funded with pre-tax money, where withdrawals are generally taxed later. Rules vary.
A retirement savings plan offered through an employer. Money is often contributed from your paycheck.
A retirement account you open on your own, outside of an employer. Common types include traditional and Roth.
A payment some investments make to the people who hold them, usually from company profits.
The increase in value when an investment is sold for more than it cost. Tax rules may apply; an advisor can explain.
A tax form that reports money taken out of a retirement account during the year.
A periodic summary of an account showing balances and activity for a time period.
The form used to name or change who would receive an account if you pass away.
also_heard_as: the form to change who gets my money
